ablations.note: 1-hop lookup ranks chains by the learned cost of the first edge and does not call algo.SSpaths. Unweighted search counts hops. DreamGraph sums learned edge costs; the published synthetic run did that sum inside HydraDB. The dict learner sums the same costs outside the engine, which is why its accuracies match.

config.protocol: score then update; drift is applied before the drift iteration's score

hypotheses.statement: On a memory replay of the synthetic ownership loop, iteration-8 DreamGraph accuracy exceeds the 1-hop first-edge ablation by at least 0.10.
On the published HydraDB run, DreamGraph's final 3-hop answer rate exceeds the unweighted walk by at least 0.50.
The dict learner matches published DreamGraph accuracy on every iteration, absolute difference under 0.005.
On the Book seller slice, the mean final learned cost of Revaluation Books is strictly below the mean final learned cost of textbooksNow.
On the Book seller slice, the dict learner matches DreamGraph on every iteration, absolute difference under 0.005.
On the Book seller slice, DreamGraph's final held-out accuracy is at least 0.75.
In the poisoned-source scenario the guard rolls back at least 3 policy versions, and the naive no-guard learner finishes at least 0.10 below DreamGraph.
Every poison rollback receipt has reason 'guard accuracy fell', a lower guard accuracy after the proposal than before, and strictly positive costs.

A model frozen after iteration 3 finishes within 0.08 of DreamGraph on the poison run, because the poison starts at iteration 4. The guard's evidence is the receipt log, not a unique final score against that frozen model.

load.what: 20 concurrent clients, each issuing 30 weighted algo.SSpaths calls against the live node.

noise.description: Synthetic chain noise. The 3-hop chain usually names the true owner; two 2-hop chains compete. Drift swaps wikidata and scraper labels and does not move the people. The answer is the person at the end of the minimum summed edge-cost path.
noise.drift_effect: wikidata and scraper labels exchange on rel_id >= drift_min_rel
noise.path_cost: sum of per-edge costs; each edge stores the learned cost of its current source

notes: Chart numbers are this document. The dashboard reads it; it does not embed a second copy.
DreamGraph, unweighted, hand-set, one-shot, greedy, and frozen answers are algo.SSpaths round trips. The dict learner is the same refit and the same sum, evaluated on plain dicts.
hop3_rate is the share of answers whose chosen path has 3 edges. Unweighted prefers the 2-hop chains.
precomputed=true means the file is an export of the object written during this run.

config.protocol: score then update; poison flag flips train feedback from the poison iteration onward; no label drift

notes: Naive fits the whole trailing window and always accepts.
Frozen-after-3 copies DreamGraph only while the poison flag is still off.
1-hop is scored with DreamGraph's guarded costs.
Receipts record guard accuracy and held-out accuracy before and after the proposal.
poison.scenario: From iteration 4 on, train feedback treats wikidata as always wrong and scraper as always right. Held-out edges and gold people do not change. A naive refit trusts the lie. The guard compares the proposal with the current policy on the last 20 questions of the window, scored against the true owner.

public.citation: Yin, Han, and Yu, TKDE 2008, claims; Dong, Berti-Equille, and Srivastava, VLDB 2009, gold author lists from book covers. Cached slice: data/book/claims.jsonl.

config.hand_set_rule: fixed volume prior, not gold accuracy
config.protocol: score then update; no label drift; same window and guard as the synthetic loop

public.encoding: Each seller is a 2-edge chain book → listing → author. Both edges carry that seller's learned cost. Path length does not depend on correctness. Unweighted search tie-breaks on node ids, and listing ids follow alphabetical seller order, so Revaluation Books wins ties when it listed the book.
public.license_note: Research distribution at https://lunadong.com/fusionDataSets.htm. See data/book/PROVENANCE.md.
public.match_rule: token Jaccard >= 0.5 on tokens longer than 2 characters, excluding 'and' and 'the'
notes: 1-hop lookup uses DreamGraph's learned costs and only the first edge. On this encoding both edges of a chain share a seller, so the sum ranks sellers the same way.
The dict learner minimizes that same sum outside HydraDB.
Seller accuracies on the full slice are descriptive. They are not written onto edges.
